claims.text: Containerless melting paired with ultra-rapid solidification can enhance the glass-forming ability of a metallic-glass precursor relative to conventional crucible-based processing.
Conventional crucible melting of metallic-glass-forming alloys is prone to heterogeneous nucleation.
Electromagnetic or aerodynamic levitation can provide containerless melting.
High cooling rates promote amorphous-metal formation.
Processing under vacuum or an inert atmosphere prevents contamination.
Processing under vacuum or an inert atmosphere reduces nucleation.
Containerless melting eliminates nucleation sites induced by contact with container walls.
Containerless melting minimizes heterogeneous nucleation centers in the melt.
Avoiding contact with container walls suppresses crystal formation.
Suppression of crystal formation extends the temperature interval over which a disordered amorphous structure is retained.
The proposed processing route can enlarge the composition range over which glass forms instead of a crystalline phase.
The proposed processing route can reduce the critical cooling rate required for glass formation.
The proposed processing route can produce a higher amorphous fraction than conventional processing.
The proposed processing route can produce a broader glass-transition range than conventional processing.
Standard crucible-based melting and quenching produces higher crystallization rates under similar conditions.
The benefit of containerless processing may be limited to alloys in which heterogeneous nucleation is a dominant crystallization pathway.
Alloys with strong intrinsic nucleation tendencies may show a smaller improvement from containerless processing.
Scaling containerless processing may present practical challenges.
